auditExceptions.why: The amplification needs an attacker-controlled pattern and optimizationLevel >= 2. Both parents pass patterns written in code, and no 3.x or 5.x fix exists. Overriding to 11.0.3 was tried on 2026-10-31 and breaks glob@7 at run time (rawGlob undefined in GlobSync._processReaddir).
auditExceptions.dropWhen: unzipper and exceljs no longer pull glob@7 and archiver, or a patched 3.x and 5.x is published.

$comment: The single definition of every version we track upstream. A Dockerfile ARG, a seam manifest, a peerDependency and a release manifest that each carried their own copy meant 'bump the pin' was four edits and one of them was always missed. Tests assert every derived copy equals the value here; the nightly compatibility matrix is one job that loops over these keys.

pandoc.notes: The document renderer's tested Linux version. Both runtime images and CI install the official architecture-specific Debian package through the same digest-checked renderer phase. Tool metadata is separate from the service contracts polled by the upstream matrix.

node.notes: DSH 0.2.2 requires Node >=24.9.0 (`engines` of @deepseek-ai/dsh). This is the newest 24 LTS at the move (2026-11-04). LoopX 1.4.0 asks for >=22.22.3 for its TypeScript control plane and for its SQLite goal store (node:sqlite, with the WAL-reset fix of SQLite 3.51.3). The control plane's own image stays on its Node 22 base: it runs no kernel.

dsh.notes: 0.2.2-rc.1 (published 2026-11-04; npm's `next`, with `latest` still 0.2.1-rc.5 at adoption), adopted on 2026-11-04 for its automation tasks that open a fresh conversation per run, on the criterion in decision #25, this version's running binary probed on the wire plus our own battery. What it moved, and what we changed for it: Node >=24.9 (the runtime image moves to 24.22.2); cordis 4.1.0, schemastery 3.19.0; 51 new wire methods classified, the forge, liveshare, action-card and plugin-recommendation namespaces denied on the proxy; tool execution is now the `tool-executor-native` row; upstream's read-before-write policy (`fs-observation-policy`) is off by default and stays off; its `deliverable-file-references` paragraph stays; the kernel's user row calls `renderSlotChain` unconditionally, which our takeover has to supply (runtimeUiTranscript.mjs); `schedule` and `ui-schedule` go on. Web Fetch no longer refuses non-public addresses upstream: `tool-web` and `web-fetch-http` stay out of this composition, as before. Earlier: the 0.2.1 line's second release candidate (published 2026-10-17T08:36:31Z; npm's `next`, with `latest` still 0.2.0-rc.2 at adoption), adopted on 2026-10-17 (R19, r19-dsh021) on the criterion in decision #25 -- this version's running binary probed on the wire plus our own battery -- not on the tag; the live run's evidence is in .evimed-local/acceptance/course-correction-20261012/live/r19-dsh021/. `publishedBefore` is COMPUTED, never typed: `node scripts/ops/kernel-install.mjs cutoff --write` resolves the closure with npm (`--package-lock-only --ignore-scripts`), reads every member's publish instant from the registry and records the latest plus one minute (here `dsh-client-ui-settings-account`, re-published 15 minutes after the CLI); `cutoff --check` (pnpm check:kernel-cutoff, the kernel-seams workflow) fails when the recorded instant is not the computed one, and scripts/ops/test/fixtures/kernel-closure-times-<version>.json replays the computation without a network; moving the pin means recording the closure it resolves to. The nightly seam check installs through the same cutoff, and the nightly `candidates` job (scripts/ops/kernel-candidate-check.mjs, report only) diffs what the dist-tags name against this pin. What moved, and what we changed for it: (1) the closure went from 278 to 295 dsh* packages (+28, -11: the client store, slots and primitives are bundled into the web frontend now, the in-process subagent driver, the hook and webhook packages and dsh-invariants left; the plugin market, cot translation, session search/titles, worktree, terminal and ralph experiments, the remote-access policy, the working-directory service and tool, the schedule tool and the DeepSeek search/fetch API provider joined); cordis 4.0.4 -> 4.0.5 (stable), schemastery 3.18.5, LibreOffice Kit 0.1.2 -> 0.1.5; the session format stays 4 (three new event types, job/registered, job/settled and working-directory/change, classified as bookkeeping) -- rolling back below this pin keeps every session written since except that 0.2.0 does not know those three types. (2) BREAKING, the subagent contract: every child is a managed activation; `subagent` answers with the child's id at once and the child's result reaches the parent as a user-role settlement notice (`source.kind: subagent-settled`), `ctx.subagents.start` and the request's `toolFilter`/`persona` are gone (a tool row carrying `toolFilter` throws), and the kernel's cancel no longer reaches children. Ours: delegations start through `startActivation` (delivery caller) with a reserved id and their mask and persona are installed in the child's own scope at `agent/created` (harness-port `startSubagent`, `installChildComposition`); the run policy counts a native child once, holds it as working until `subagent/end`, keeps the root's turn open until every child it started has settled (so the notice is read in the same turn and the run is not finished while a child works), stops children with a cancelled turn under the kernel's human authority, and refuses a settlement-only step after a cancel; the kernel's per-tree cap (8) takes the run's concurrency budget (`subagent.maxActiveSubagents`). `session/wait` is the DSH SDK's JSON-RPC protocol; nothing of ours speaks it. (3) The persona may not name `{{cwd}}` any more (only `provider` and `model` are prompt variables): the working-directory service states the directory in the runtime context. (4) Rows decided by value: `schedule` (and `ui-schedule` hidden), `tool-working-directory`, `harness-dev-context`, `web-deepseek-api` and `web-search-deepseek` disabled; `remote-access`, `working-directory`, `ui-secret-mask` and `ui-deepseek-model-label-1017` kept. The dump-config baseline was re-recorded (208 rows) after the seeding at the OLD pins reproduced the committed baseline byte for byte. (5) Seven wire methods are new and classified (`pluginMarket/*` and `cotTranslation/*` also denied on the proxy, `remoteAccess/follow` open there, `terminal/attach`); three terminal methods retired; the seam check reads 0.2.1's structured remote-info object as well as the old endpoint ids. (6) Frame layer: the slot contracts and class suffixes were re-read; the shipped answer row and model seat now declare child slots, which the frame kit no longer refuses to take over; the composer's statistics are per-pill dock entries (`data-composer-stat`); panel remotes are read from each package's `./client` export (dsh-client-connection serves client.browser.js); packages/contracts/dsh/{panel-remotes,client-locale}.json re-recorded. (7) The golden frames were re-recorded from a live kernel with a real model (golden-diff-report.txt in the evidence directory). (8) dsh-skill-office no longer ships its structural checker script; ours is runtime/skills/office/shared/office_check.py. (9) The LoopX plugin (0.1.1-beta.6) declares `<0.2.1-0`: it runs under the kernel's exact-version exemption (`loopx.compatibility.dshVersionExemption`). `dsh plugin` manages a profile with pnpm and writes a pnpm-workspace.yaml listing the profile itself, which pnpm 9 refuses to add into without -w; this pin tracks DSH's own packageManager, not the workspace's. Upstream also tags prereleases on GitHub that npm never receives, so the matrix reports the GitHub tag as `upstreamTag` beside the npm `latest`: npm is what is installable and what `behind` means, the tag is the early warning. Moved from 0.2.1-rc.2 to 0.2.1-rc.5 on 2026-11-01 (npm's `latest` and `next` since 2026-10-29; rc.3 and rc.4 were never adopted alone; 0.2.2-alpha.2 exists on the `alpha` tag and is not followed): the closure grew by one package (307 members: dsh-client-ui-entry-customization), 24 packages changed in content and the rest are byte-identical, among them the sandbox, jobs, agent loop, subagent, session and tool packages and the remote wire. What changed: (1) the DeepSeek Messages transport gained a model listing (GET /models, cached, 5 s deadline) that the api-key route follows only for the official origin with the built-in catalogue, so this deployment's gateway route follows none (no listing line in any live kernel log), and the built-in catalogue states 1,048,576 as the context window; (2) the web app mounts a new row, `entry-customization` (the More menus: browse plugins, create a plugin), hidden by the hosted profile and paired in hiddenPanelsHaveAMethodBan; (3) the MCP client answers an empty resource list for a server without the resources capability instead of asking it; (4) the chat strips a <signature> prefix from reasoning text for display, New Session reuses a blank of the workspace, and desktop-only analytics events were added (the telemetry rows stay disabled). Recorded live on rc.5 with real DeepSeek: the composition (210 rows; the seeded dump equalled the committed record except the one new row), the golden frames and the settings document; panel remotes and client dictionaries from the closure; the frame layer's pins moved after the eight changed client bundles were compared with their rc.2 text (no slot we occupy and no hashed class suffix changed). The live run covered a plain reply, a tool turn, a sub-agent whose settlement arrives inside the root's turn, a cancel with a background job (the job killed, no turn of its own afterwards), ask-user in the frame, a control-plane session opened by id and prompted, and a LoopX goal with pause, resume and a continuation turn under the exemption. Bundles beside the kernel: dsh-mermaid 0.4.2 -> 0.4.4 (client fixes, same patch rows); dsh-cite stays at 0.3.5 (0.7.x declares dsh >=0.2.1-rc.3 and brings a workbench client, a locked file store and an updater of its own: a different product, to be adopted on its own evidence); the OpenViking memory plugin stays at 0.5.26 (the pin follows the engine's tag line and 0.5.31 is in no tag); the LoopX plugin 0.1.1-beta.6 is still the newest plugin release.

annotationCompatibility.reason: The bundle picks its interface language by an exact match of the kernel's locale id (zh, en, ru; every other id is English, which its own test pins for fr, de and zh-Hans), and the product's locale id is zh-x-evimed: the annotation toolbar, its editor and the block it writes into the prompt turned English on the pin that brought 1.4.11. The edit makes it choose by the primary language subtag (zh-x-evimed -> zh); nothing else in the bundle changes.
annotationCompatibility.upgradePath: A build-time, digest-bound one-line edit of the pinned bundle's client.js (deploy/runtime-dsh/annotation-compat.mjs); a changed byte fails the image build by name, and the edit applied over its own output verifies the reverse transformation first. Drop it, and this record, when the bundle takes a regional or private-use tag of a language it ships as that language (the same defect for any Chinese-reading node, worth saying upstream), or when the product's locale is registered under an id the bundle takes as it is. Re-review on every annotation pin change; the sha256 is of the reviewed file.

upstreamDefects.$comment: Behaviour of the pinned kernel that we cannot patch (never node_modules, never the kernel) and work around at the narrowest place we own. Measured on the runtime image with the real launcher and the production container flags on 2026-10-31, in the benchmark round of 2026-10-29; each entry names where it lives upstream, what we do about it, and when the workaround can go.

sandboxWritableRoots.where: @deepseek-ai/dsh-sandbox-local lib/index.js, landlockProfileArgs: the Landlock launcher is given `--ro /`, `--rw /dev/null`, and under workspace-write `--rw /tmp` and `--rw <workspace>`, spelled as literals. Unlike the Seatbelt rung and the in-process file fence they do not follow os.tmpdir() (dsh-sandbox writableRoots), and the launcher reads no environment variable (@deepseek-ai/node-addon-system lib/index.js: none by design).
sandboxWritableRoots.what: Every bash-tool command runs where only /tmp, the workspace and /dev/null are writable. The kernel's own TMPDIR (/runtime/tmp, the project volume, so its spill files do not fill the 64 MiB tmpfs) is therefore a directory its commands cannot write: `Rscript -e` fails with "creating temporary file for '-e' failed" and LibreOffice Kit's render with EACCES on mkdtemp. /dev/shm is not writable either (worked around, see `ours`), so Python multiprocessing (SemLock via sem_open), joblib/loky process pools and numba's parallel initialisation fail ("joblib will operate in serial mode", "Could not obtain multiprocessing lock"); threads are unaffected. A command cannot write /proc/self/oom_score_adj. The XDG directories under /runtime, which hold the kernel's configuration, are read-only to commands by the same rule, and that stays.
sandboxWritableRoots.ours: LoopX's own directory: deploy/runtime-dsh/evimed-landlock-run.sh also grants `--rw /runtime/home/.loopx` under workspace-write (made and checked for a symlink by the serve script, asserted by check-tool-sandbox.sh), because `loopx bootstrap` run by the model was blocked-write-denied on it and the model improvised another HOME, so 40-85% of a goal's tool calls were the goal's own machinery and the bar could not see the goal (drills of 2026-11-03). deploy/runtime-dsh/evimed-tool-env.sh (BASH_ENV, exported by the serve script) points TMPDIR at /tmp for the commands only; the launch plan sets MPLCONFIGDIR and NUMBA_CACHE_DIR under /tmp; deploy/runtime-dsh/evimed-oom-guard.sh raises the commands' oom_score_adj from outside the sandbox. /dev/shm: WORKED AROUND (2026-11-01) by the kernel's one supported override, the `sandbox` row's `runnerCommand`: packages/socket/cordis.patch.yml names deploy/runtime-dsh/evimed-landlock-run.sh (installed at /usr/local/lib/evimed/evimed-landlock-run by the three runtime image recipes) and the launcher's fatal lines as `runnerFailureSignatures`; the row is baked into the sealed profile, so an older image keeps the kernel's own runner and the control plane's patch is not involved. The runner accepts exactly the two profiles dsh-sandbox-local 0.2.1 builds (read-only, workspace-write; recorded from the installed kernel in deploy/runtime-dsh/fixtures/sandbox-profile.json and re-checked by verify-harness-seams), refuses any other argument by name (exit 125, `evimed-landlock-run: ...`), grants what the kernel's own Landlock runner grants plus `--rw /dev/shm`, and `exec`s the same launcher, so pid, process group, signals, exit status, standard streams and environment are the launcher's own (the one difference: dash records PWD in the environment of a command that is not bash). The kernel records a custom runner's enforcement as `full` without asking the host; the startup self-check therefore reads the launcher's partial-enforcement line itself (harness-port `probeSandbox`), so a profile that requires `full` still refuses a host that cannot give it (shown on a partial-ABI host with OPEN_SCIENCE_RUNTIME_SANDBOX_ENFORCEMENT=full). A kernel that stops granting a pool's semaphores another way, or changes the profile, is noticed by that check, by apps/server/test/runtimeLandlockRunner.test.mjs and by deploy/runtime-dsh/check-tool-sandbox.sh, which now asserts /dev/shm writable, a Pool, a ProcessPoolExecutor and joblib workers on the built image, and the build smoke asserts the first two where the builder can enforce Landlock. Size: /dev/shm is Docker's default 64 MiB tmpfs in the runtime container (the launch plan sets no --shm-size and none was added: the default equals the 64 MiB /tmp); it counts against the container's memory limit; a write past its end fails with ENOSPC, and touching a page of an mmap'ed segment past it ends the process with SIGBUS (the pool reports a broken worker); what a pool killed with SIGKILL leaves there stays until the runtime container is removed.
sandboxWritableRoots.checkedAtRc5: Re-read at 0.2.1-rc.5 (2026-11-01): dsh-sandbox-local, dsh-sandbox, dsh-sandbox-policy and node-addon-system are byte-identical to rc.2 (compared file by file across the two installed closures), so landlockProfileArgs still grants only /dev/null, /tmp and the workspace and there is no writable-roots setting; reproduced on a live rc.5 kernel through the model's bash tool (multiprocessing.Pool: PermissionError [Errno 13] in SemLock.__init__), and fixed there by the runner above (Pool and ProcessPoolExecutor return, a write outside the grants and to /proc is still refused).
sandboxWritableRoots.upgradePath: Ask upstream for the roots to follow the policy (os.tmpdir() and /dev/shm in landlockProfileArgs, or a sandbox-policy list of extra writable roots). When it lands: delete the `sandbox` row in packages/socket/cordis.patch.yml, deploy/runtime-dsh/evimed-landlock-run.sh, its three COPY lines and the two chmods (Dockerfile, Dockerfile.delta, Dockerfile.agentbay, install-runtime.sh), deploy/runtime-dsh/fixtures/sandbox-profile.json, scripts/ops/sandbox-profile.mjs with its block in verify-harness-seams.mjs and the kernel-seams path triggers, apps/server/test/runtimeLandlockRunner.test.mjs, the `sandbox.config.*` invariants in kernelDefaults.test.mjs, the partial-line read in harness-port probeSandbox (with packages/harness-port/test/sandboxProbe.test.mjs) and the runner's use in check-tool-sandbox.sh and build-smoke.sh; re-record the composition baseline; delete evimed-tool-env.sh's TMPDIR case too when TMPDIR is granted; re-measure on the image with deploy/runtime-dsh/check-tool-sandbox.sh and the probes in apps/server/test/runtimeToolEnv.test.mjs (EVIMED_LANDLOCK_RUN names the launcher).

jobKillProcessGroup.where: @deepseek-ai/dsh-subprocess-local lib/runner-launch-*.js: spawnSubprocess starts the command `detached` (its own session and group) and fallbackOwner.signal / signalTree deliver SIGTERM and then SIGKILL as kill(-pgid); the kernel's job_kill (dsh-jobs-local killJob -> dsh-tool-bash processJob.cancel -> proc.kill -> terminate) and a cancelled foreground call are the same path. SIGKILL is skipped when the group is empty (`alive()` is kill(-pgid, 0)).
jobKillProcessGroup.what: Containment is by process group only (there is no systemd scope in a container). A descendant that leaves the group is not signalled, and an empty group reads as stopped: GNU timeout calls setpgid(0, 0), so in a pipeline (`timeout 3000 python train.py 2>&1 | tail`, which bash forks, unlike a lone command that it execs as the group leader) job_kill answered "requested cancellation", the group was empty a moment later, and the command ran on until the model ran kill -9 (ResearchClawBench Life_000). setsid, bash job control and Python's start_new_session escape the same way, and are not covered. A process started with `nohup cmd &` stays in the group, is not a registered job, and its death (OOM-killed, or killed with the group) is reported to nobody (Neuroscience_003).
jobKillProcessGroup.ours: deploy/runtime-dsh/tool-bin/timeout, first on PATH in the commands' shells (evimed-tool-env.sh): a bash wrapper that stays in the signalled group and forwards the signal to the real timeout, which signals the command and its tree. Covers timeout only; reproduced and fixed on the image with the real launcher.
jobKillProcessGroup.upgradePath: Upstream should signal the descendants it can find (the session id, the cgroup, or a walk of /proc children) and treat a non-empty session as alive. When it does, delete tool-bin/timeout and its PATH entry.

customRunnerFailureNoExitGate.where: @deepseek-ai/dsh-sandbox-local lib/index.js and @deepseek-ai/dsh-sandbox classifyRunnerFailure: a settled command is read against the active backend's runner-failure rules, each of which requires a non-zero exit and may carry an `allowedExitCodes` gate. The kernel's own Landlock rule is gated by the launcher's failure exit code; the rule built from a `sandbox` row's `runnerFailureSignatures` is `[{ fatalSignatures: <the list> }]` and the setting offers no exit-code field.
customRunnerFailureNoExitGate.what: With a custom runner (our `sandbox.runnerCommand`), a command that fails by its own doing and whose stderr contains one of the signatures (`landlock-run: exec failed` is what the launcher prints when the command it was asked to run cannot be executed; `evimed-landlock-run: ` is ours) reads as a thrown SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE ("refusing to run the command unconfined. Runner failure: ...") instead of an ordinary non-zero result. Exit 0 cannot trigger it (the classifier returns nothing for 0 and for a signal), the command has already run under the launcher's confinement, and nothing is ever run unconfined: the cost is a misleading refusal message on a command the model could have corrected, not a hole in the sandbox.
customRunnerFailureNoExitGate.ours: Nothing beyond choosing the signatures narrowly (packages/socket/cordis.patch.yml lists the launcher's fatal lines and our own prefix, not a generic word) and reading the exit status in harness-port `probeSandbox` for the startup self-check (a non-zero exit of `true` is a probe error).
customRunnerFailureNoExitGate.upgradePath: Ask upstream for an exit-code field beside `runnerFailureSignatures` (the `allowedExitCodes` the built-in rules already carry), then set it to the launcher's failure exit and the runner's 125 in packages/socket/cordis.patch.yml and re-record the composition baseline.

openlist.notes: Self-hosted drive aggregator; v4.2.6 (2026-09-01), including access-control and authentication fixes from the current stable release. EviMed uses the pinned list, get and link contracts, then reads bytes through OpenList's same-origin proxy without following a provider-controlled redirect. The service runs with an isolated data volume and tenant-prefixed paths.

evimed-extract.recordedAgainst: the parser team's test environment (its address is not published; a deployment names its parser in OPEN_SCIENCE_DOCUMENT_PARSER_URL)
evimed-extract.notes: The team's own document-parsing API (API.md v1.0.0 of 2026-10-27, develop at 7f79242), which replaced the self-hosted MinerU container outright on 2026-09-20 and replaced its own routes on 2026-10-27: the single-engine /api/v1/extract/text/file and /api/v1/parse/file now answer 404, and the routes are POST /api/v1/parse/engine-a/file and /engine-b/file (engine A: page markers, parse_info, OCR, every format we read; engine B: higher quality, fewer formats, no parse_info; the service never switches between them, OPEN_SCIENCE_DOCUMENT_PARSER_ENGINE chooses). Every business route needs a Bearer key its own console issues (OPEN_SCIENCE_DOCUMENT_PARSER_TOKEN_FILE) with the scope `parse` for the text and `extract` for the optional metadata. When the service cannot answer for a PDF, Word, slides or workbook the same text is read from the original bytes in the runtime controller's intake container (documentLocalReader.mjs, labelled evimed-local-reader / local-fallback). `revision` is the label the knowledge-base index is keyed by, together with each file's SHA-256, and a document keeps the label it was parsed under: moving it affects documents parsed from now on. The service is not polled by the nightly matrix (there is no release feed to poll); the contract fixtures are the documented answers of API.md v1.0.0 (nothing could be recorded: the key was refused when this was written), and `scripts/ops/record-parser-contract.mjs` records the real ones once a working key exists.

openviking.notes: The context engine of the base stack, used three ways since v0.5.0 (2026-10-13; packages/contracts/openviking/README.md is the division of labour, capability by capability). (1) The derived recall index it has been since 2026-09-11: it ranks the research-memory records and the capsule facts whose authoritative rows stay in the control-plane PostgreSQL, under `memories/evimed/` — its `write` offers replace/append/create and no compare-and-swap, so the `expectedVersion` the record store enforces has no equivalent and those records are never its own. (2) Native memory: the engine extracts an account's memory from sessions with its own templates (deploy/web/openviking/memory-templates, eight types, the platform's keep / never-keep policy written in the engine's template language) and the official DSH plugin `plugin` reads it. (3) Knowledge: documents pushed as resources and compiled by the built-in VikingBot with the two official skills in `skills` into wiki pages and a graph. (2) and (3) are original data, so the volume is backed up (docs/WEB_OPERATIONS_RUNBOOK.md) and a rollback is a restore, never a downgrade: a v0.5.0 write is not readable by v0.4.x, nor a v0.5.1.1 write by v0.5.0 (the task store has no migration code, so the switch is made with no task in flight). Moved from v0.5.0 on 2026-10-23: v0.5.1 itself is excluded (its second and later commits of one session were not searchable until v0.5.1.1, PR #6331, and nativeTurnCommit commits one session once per attended turn). Moved to v0.5.3 on 2026-11-05 (v0.5.2, v0.5.2.1 and v0.5.3 read at the tags' source and the wheels; the 0.5.2.x line is skipped because v0.5.3 contains it): `content/batch-write` lost `expected_sha256` (PR #6615 - the operation model forbids unknown keys, so the v0.5.1.1 checked write is a 4xx there), which `OpenVikingResources.writePage` now makes up for by reading the page first; the compile-scope proof's hashes are those of the v0.5.3 wheel; `compile --skill memory` over the memories root fails at v0.5.3 (measured on the rehearsal engine, 2026-11-05, on a throwaway and two real accounts: MEMORY_CONSOLIDATION_FAILED, memory write target must be inside a memory type directory; the runner accepts the root and its own write check refuses it - an upstream defect at the tag), while a type directory (preferences, preferences/self, recent_work) completes, so nativeMemoryConsolidation.mjs walks the type directories that hold two or more files, one task at a time, never observations/ (its notes are counted a conversation to a line) or evimed/, and a root consolidation can return when upstream fixes it; no path this deployment reads moved in the source (account store, sessions, memories, resources), but the first start writes new things to the volume (the system-asset sync copies the packaged compile skills and memory templates into each account's viking://system/ and records a manifest, and the compile target state is keyed by destination URI), and whether a production volume opens and stays readable by the pin before it is only a rehearsal's to say, so a rollback is a restore here as everywhere. MODEL PATH: the engine's `vlm` is this deployment's own model gateway, with a service bearer (`OPEN_SCIENCE_OPENVIKING_MODEL_KEY_FILE`), thinking off, non-streaming for extraction and summaries and streaming for the Compile agent; nothing in such a request names a user, so the spend is the platform's, booked to the internal project `evimed-openviking` under `memory-extraction` (root vlm) and `knowledge` (the Compile agent's own bearer, derived from the same key) and held by `OPEN_SCIENCE_OPENVIKING_MODEL_DAILY_BUDGET_CNY`. The engine classifies a model error by its body code (upstream source at the tag): a spent budget is answered 402 `insufficient_quota`, which it reads as an exhausted quota and does not retry; a refusal it does not recognise is retried up to `vlm.max_retries` (3), as is a 429/5xx — v0.5.0 ended the commit on any 4xx. IDENTITY: since v0.5.1 the server forwards the caller's account and user to its Compile runtime itself, so the identity shim of the v0.5.0 pin (deploy/web/openviking/identity_shim.py, its entrypoint wrapper, `compile_api.base_url`, the `compileShim` fact) is deleted and the rendered ov.conf has no `compile_api` section; the server then looks at its Compile runtime every 30 s (a finished compile is seen up to 30 s late). A compile naming another user's root is refused at submission (403) but one naming `viking://resources/…` or `viking://agent/…` is accepted, so `OpenVikingResources.submitCompile` refuses every root outside the acting user's own resources. LIMITS MEASURED ON THE v0.5.1.1 LAB (2026-10-23, not yet re-measured at v0.5.3; packages/contracts/openviking/README.md has them with their evidence): there is no cap on the typed pages of a compile target any more (a target of 140 existing pages was compiled twice: every page kept byte for byte, no stub, and the platform's own stop at 100 typed pages is removed with it); a compile that says `completed` can be partial (a failed pipeline job leaves `meta.pipeline.errors` and a "Partial output" warning) and two of nine runs over the three-document fixture corpus wrote only index.md with no warning; `content/write` has no version precondition but `content/batch-write` does (`expected_sha256` per operation: 409 `Content revision changed`, or `path_busy` while a directory is processed), which is how a page is written back; tokens are reported under `meta.pipeline.tokens`; a failed extraction commit is not retried by the server for a recognised quota code and the overlay replays it; task records expire after 24 h (7 d when failed); an OVPack carries no `k=v` tags. `skills.<name>.upstreamSha256` is the file at the tag (shipped as apps/server/src/openVikingSkills/<name>.skill.md, Apache-2.0); `installedSha256` is what the server stores after re-wrapping the frontmatter and dropping the final newline (`SkillLoader.parse` then `to_skill_md`: yaml.dump of name, description and any allowed-tools, tags and metadata, `---`, a blank line and the stripped body; unchanged between v0.5.1.1 and v0.5.3, and it reproduces the v0.5.1.1 value of both skills byte for byte), and is what the startup check compares (`openVikingEngine.mjs`). From v0.5.3 `llm-wiki` is shipped as a system asset (`openviking/system_assets/compile/example-skills/llm-wiki/SKILL.md`, which the server also copies into each account's `viking://system/compile/example-skills/`); `knowledge-graph` stays at `examples/compile/ov-compile-skills/` with the same blob, and both are still installed under `viking://agent/skills` by the startup check. `plugin` is the version in examples/dsh-memory-plugin/package.json at the tag (0.5.31 at v0.5.3; 0.5.26 at v0.5.1 and v0.5.1.1; v0.5.0 carried 0.5.20, so the engine and the plugin sit on one tag line since this move; 0.5.27 and 0.5.28 are on npm only, in no tag, and stay out); it has no runtime npm dependencies and its bundle row `openviking-memory-runtime` is inserted by its own cordis.patch.yml. `embedding` is what `scripts/ops/configure-production-state.mjs` renders into ov.conf (provider `dashscope` with `input: "text"`, which appends `/compatible-mode/v1` to `apiBase` itself and is the only provider that sends `dimensions`); changing the model or the dimension invalidates every stored vector, so it takes a `pnpm rebuild:memory-index --all` for the derived part and a reindex of the rest. `rerank` is read by the control plane, not by the server: `/search/find` never reranks, so the reranker runs where the hydrated text already is and the ov.conf carries no rerank section. A find score is (cosine + 1) / 2 since v0.4.22 and unchanged at v0.5.0 (production volume rehearsed 2026-10-12: same entries, same hits, scores = (old + 1) / 2) and at v0.5.1.1 (the same four fixture records score the same four numbers; not re-measured at v0.5.3, whose retrieval code differs only in where a rerank threshold applies and there is no rerank section), so `OPEN_SCIENCE_MEMORY_SEARCH_MIN_SCORE` stays 0.75. The server is AGPL-3.0 and runs unmodified as its own service; the CLI, plugins, skills and examples are Apache-2.0. The container tag carries a `v` prefix the PyPI version does not; the unprefixed tag does not exist and a compose file that names it fails at pull. Releases land every few days and have moved data layouts before, so the pin moves only through the matrix and the contract fixtures.

pgvector.notes: The control plane's PostgreSQL image since 2026-09-20: the official postgres:16 bookworm image with the pgvector extension added, so the data directory (/var/lib/postgresql/data) carries over from postgres:16.14-bookworm unchanged. Needed by the knowledge-base index's vector leg; without the extension that leg is skipped and kb_search answers mode "keyword", nothing fails. 0.8.x rather than earlier because 0.8 added iterative index scans, which keep a filtered nearest-neighbour search (one account's documents out of everyone's) from returning fewer rows than asked for. Read off Docker Hub on 2026-09-19: 0.8.6-pg16-bookworm is the newest 0.8.x tag, its image config says PG_VERSION=16.15-1.pgdg12+2 (not below production's 16.14), and the digests are the index and the linux/amd64 manifest. The extension is not marked trusted, which is fine here: the image entrypoint creates POSTGRES_USER as a superuser, so the application's migration creates it on first start and the backup restore drill can recreate it; pg_trgm (trusted, part of every postgres image) is created the same way. Moving this pin is a host step as well as a PR: back up, swap the image, and let the migration or the operator run CREATE EXTENSION.

knowledge-plugin.notes: The knowledge-source plugin (evimed-knowledge-plugin): the plugin team's own service that owns everything between the outside world and a normalised entry for the frontier feed (「前沿动态」) — the source registry, scheduling, fetching, parsing, per-source de-duplication, enrichment and source health — and that the control plane only ever pulls from (apps/server/src/knowledgePluginClient.mjs; the plugin never calls the platform). What is pinned here is the contract, not a build: `version` is the OpenAPI document's own version, whose canonical copy lives with the plan in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-21-medical-frontier-feed-assets/contract/ and is vendored byte for byte as `contractFile`, a test holding the two equal. The image is the plugin team's: until they have a registry it is built on the serving host from 项目代码/knowledge-plugin by scripts/ops/host-knowledge-plugin-build.sh, tagged with the plugin's own version and the release it was built from, and named in the deployment's .env as EVIMED_KNOWLEDGE_PLUGIN_IMAGE (deploy/web/docker-compose.knowledge.yml refuses to start without it), so no build is written here. The platform checks the contract major: the client compares the manifest's contract.version with OPEN_SCIENCE_KNOWLEDGE_PLUGIN_MIN_CONTRACT (default 1.0 — the same major, at least that minor), and the stream of a plugin speaking another major is not pulled until its manifest names a compatible contract again, while readiness warns frontier_plugin_incompatible and never turns red. Within major 1 the contract only grows (its rule 1), so a minor bump is additive and the platform ignores what it does not know yet. Moving this pin is re-vendoring the YAML and re-recording the fixtures off a live plugin with packages/contracts/knowledge-plugin/fixtures/record.mjs — never editing a fixture by hand. 1.3.0 (2026-10-05, flywheel F09) added one field to a source row, `platform_produced`: the source's content is the platform's own (the evidence feed the plugin reads like any other publisher's); the platform shows its items as 「EviMed 出品」 and never counts them as independent corroboration. A minor only adds, so the stream's recordings stayed as recorded and `record.mjs --platform-source` recorded again only what the minor changes (manifest, health and the one source row), off a live plugin of 1.3.0, which provenance.json says (`partialRecordings`). 1.4.0 (2026-10-10, review D-10) added one field to the health answer, `host_budget`: today's (UTC) requests against each host's own daily cap, `{host: {used, cap}}`. A spent cap makes the plugin refuse that host's polls until 00:00 UTC as its own decision, which counts against no source's health, so the table is the only place the spend shows; the platform exports it as open_science_frontier_plugin_host_budget_used / _cap and alerts on FrontierHostBudgetNearCap (used / cap > 0.9 for thirty minutes). It also states what `last_ok_fetch_at` counts: a 204, or a body with nothing in it, is the source's failure and not a read, where a page that parsed to no entries still is. Again a minor only adds, so the stream's recordings and the source row stayed as recorded and `record.mjs --host-budget` recorded again the manifest and the health answer, off a live plugin of 1.4.0, which provenance.json says (`partialRecordings`). There is no release feed to poll: the nightly matrix reports the upstream as unknown and replays the recorded fixtures at the pin (contractAtPin). 1.5.0 (2026-10-22, fr-social) added social posts: Entry.channel (every entry from then on), platform, author, media (stored images the plugin serves at GET /v1/media/{id}, re-encoded, at most 1.5 MB, a 3 GB store evicting the least recently served), quoted and metrics; EntryText.body_text (the full text, 40,000 characters); Health.providers (each paid provider's calls, spend, daily cap and balance — SocialData, Dajiala, the GEO crawler) and Health.discovery (fr-sources' daily counts), and POST /v1/sources/screening (fr-sources); the read methods socialdata, dajiala and social-crawl. The brief named it 1.4.0, which host_budget had already taken. A minor only adds, so `record.mjs --social` recorded again only the manifest, the health answer, one X post, one WeChat article, their texts and one image, off a local plugin that read them live once (provenance.json, `partialRecordings`). 1.5.1 (2026-10-22, rt-papers) widened EntryText.fetched_from with the paper text chain's steps (openalex, landing, publisher-feed, europepmc-fulltext, elsevier) and says a full text writes its section headings as `## ` paragraphs; `record.mjs --patch` recorded again only the manifest and the health answer, off a local plugin of 1.5.1 (crawler off). 1.6.0 (2026-10-24, ct-mix) added POST /v1/leads: the addresses the platform's lead triggers found (apps/server/src/frontierLeads.mjs: a daily watch, a congress calendar, genre gaps, event follow-ups, searched through the web-search gateway under the feed's purpose and budget), which the plugin reads under its own rules and emits as ordinary entries under the registered source of the site, account or journal, else under a lead source of its own (the read method `lead`, never polled), naming the site a discovery candidate of line `lead`; Health.leads and Manifest.capabilities.leads say it is served. It is the platform's one write to the plugin and changes nothing of rule 6 (the plugin still never calls the platform). A plugin older than 1.6.0 answers the post 404, which the lead triggers count as a failure and nothing else. `record.mjs --leads` recorded again the manifest, the health answer and two posts to /v1/leads off a local plugin over an empty database (crawler off), keeping the 1.5.1 health answer and manifest, which named the paid providers with a live run's calls and the populated fields, as health-1.5.1.json and manifest-1.5.1.json. 1.7.0 (2026-10-25, c2-leads) added GET /v1/hot-lists: the public hot lists the plugin reads on its own pacing every 30 minutes (Baidu's realtime board, Toutiao's hot board, Weibo's hot search, English Wikipedia's most-viewed articles and Google Trends' US trending searches, the last two through the relay) and keeps 72 hours — ranks, titles, heat, the board's description and link, never a post or an account — which the platform's hot-event trigger reads (apps/server/src/frontierTopics.mjs) to find the public events that raise a medical question; Health.hot_lists (each board's last good read and last error) and Manifest.capabilities.hot_lists say it is served. The plugin still judges nothing and calls nobody. `record.mjs --hot-lists` recorded again the manifest and the health answer, the hot lists a live round read (the relay boards failing by name where no relay is configured) and a refused since, off a local plugin (crawler off), keeping the 1.6.0 health answer and manifest, which counted the recorded lead posts, as health-1.6.0.json and manifest-1.6.0.json.

dashscope.notes: The independent reviewer (plan 2026-09-22, tiered review): Qwen3.8-Max on DashScope's OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint, called by the control plane only (apps/server/src/reviewModel.mjs) with the operator's DashScope key file — the runtime holds no key. The snapshot is pinned, not the parent `qwen3.8-max`, because whatever the reviewer's findings are calibrated against is a version. Recorded on the live wire on 2026-09-23 (packages/contracts/dashscope/fixtures): `/models` lists `qwen3.8-max` and `qwen3.8-max-0902`; the dated alias `qwen3.8-max-2026-09-02` answers as `qwen3.8-max-0902`; an unknown snapshot is 404 `model_not_found`; thinking is on when `enable_thinking` is absent; `enable_thinking: false` and `thinking_budget` are honoured without streaming; strict `json_schema` is honoured with thinking on and off; reasoning tokens are counted in `completion_tokens` (`completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens`); cached prompt tokens are `prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens`. With thinking off the model paraphrased an `evidence` field instead of copying it — the verbatim check lives in code (@evimed/domain reviewFindings). Price (the model's page, 2026-09-23): input ¥12, output ¥36, implicit-cache hit ¥1.5 per million tokens, no night rate — REFERENCE_PRICE_LIST evimed-reference-2026-09-23. thinkingBudget 16000 (raised from 8000 the same day): both live editor passes over a real 64 KB package spent all 8,000 reasoning tokens, and the two answered differently — 13 findings and no checklist, then 4 findings and all 19 checklist items; a 3-claim package spends 1.4–2.7k, so the ceiling only binds where it was binding.

typesafe.notes: TypeSafe's Jev (a System One model: typed questions over a text state, answered with probabilities; it generates no text) as the first pass of the reply check, L1 (apps/server/src/replyCheckJev.mjs, jevModel.mjs; the owner's decision of 2026-09-24). Called by the control plane only, with the operator's key file (OPEN_SCIENCE_TYPESAFE_API_KEY_FILE, mounted from OPEN_SCIENCE_TYPESAFE_API_KEY_HOST_FILE; unset binds /dev/null, which is no key and Jev off) — the runtime holds no key. The exact version is pinned, never `jev-latest`: TypeSafe's own models page says to pin the version a confidence threshold was tuned against, config.mjs refuses a pin that is not jev-X.Y.Z, and the client discards an answer from any other version. `supportConfidence` 0.8 is that threshold: a cited sentence Jev answers `supports` at or above it, naming no medicine, is recorded supported without a reviewer call; every other sentence goes to Qwen3.8-Max as before. Measured twice on the 101 claim/quote pairs of the 2026-09-21 probe (40 real matrix rows, 40 wrong-sentence, 11 changed-number, 10 negated): pairwise that day 98/101 exact; in the shipped form on 2026-09-24 — about fifty pairs to a request, each sentence with its own sources under its own key, every wrong-sentence pair in the same request as the passage that truly supports it — 100/101 exact, and at 0.8 Jev settled 37 of the 40 true supports with no false settlement. The one false `supports` sat at confidence 0.73 (0.64 pairwise); a gate of 0.7 would have settled it. Confidence is (k·p_max − 1)/(k − 1) of the answer's own probabilities (docs.typesafe.ai/confidence), and code re-derives it before it gates anything. `maxRequestTokens` and `maxStateTokens` are the provider's ceilings (docs.typesafe.ai/models, 2026-09-24: 64k per request, 32k for the state plus the longest question); a request estimated over either is not sent, and the reviewer judges every sentence. Price: $0.042 per million input tokens, output free, no night rate — REFERENCE_PRICE_LIST evimed-reference-2026-09-24, converted at the CFETS central parity it fixes. Wire (packages/contracts/typesafe/fixtures, recorded 2026-09-24; first seen 2026-09-21): an answer carries `model`, `answers` and `usage.input_tokens`/`output_tokens`; no key is 403 and a wrong key 401, both `authentication_error` (the documentation lists 401 only); a malformed request and an unknown model are 400 `api_usage_error` (the documentation says 422); no rate-limit or request-id headers; 0.2–1.0 s. Jev's documented weak spots — counting, numeric closeness, dates, a state full of material the question does not need, and a state that addresses the checker — are why it may only confirm support: it never raises a ⚠, never judges a medicine sentence, and nothing it says authorizes anything. Moving the pin is re-recording the fixtures with packages/contracts/typesafe/fixtures/record.mjs and re-measuring the gate on the same corpus.

deepseek.notes: The research model: DeepSeek's OpenAI-compatible chat API, reached only through the control plane's model gateway (apps/server/src/modelGateway.mjs) — the runtime holds no key. `model` is what a deployment runs when OPEN_SCIENCE_DEEPSEEK_MODEL is unset, and what the release receipt certifies end to end; `certified` is the gateway's allowlist (`supportedDeepSeekModels`): readiness refuses to serve and the runtime refuses to launch on any other name. Until 2026-09-27 the model was written only in the gateway, config.mjs, .env.example and compose, with nothing holding them equal (platform audit I1-13); packages/contracts/deepseek now does, together with the frontier and memory-extraction defaults and the specialist engines' LLM_MODEL. Moving the pin is one edit here plus the gateway's constants, and a new release receipt against the new model. From DSH 0.1.7 the kernel reaches the model through the gateway's Anthropic Messages route (/internal/model/v1/messages -> DeepSeek's /anthropic/v1/messages), the only protocol 0.1.7's DeepSeek adapter speaks; the control plane's own callers stay on chat/completions. Both routes reserve and settle through the same usage ledger. 2026-10-17: `deepseek-flash` is served by DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 from that day, under the same name, method and price. Verified the same day: GET /models answered deepseek-flash and deepseek-v4-pro to the controller's probe with this key; DeepSeek's own 'Your First API Call' page, read through its Fetch API while recording the tool fixtures (apps/server/test/fixtures/deepseek-tools/recorded-2026-10-17.json), says deepseek-flash 'is now served by DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017, and the calling method remains unchanged', and that deepseek-v4-flash and deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp are still accepted, served by it and billed at the Flash price. The gateway's certification compares nothing beyond the model id: `supportedDeepSeekModels` holds names, the release receipt names the configured model, and the provider's own `model` field is recorded on each ledger row (observed_model) and never compared -- so `model`, `certified` and the price rows do not move; a release receipt signed before 2026-10-17 certified the earlier model behind the same name, and the next one certifies this one. The same day DeepSeek opened two tool APIs, `tools`: Search answers in the web-search gateway beside SearXNG and Bailian, Fetch is web_read's second reader (apps/server/src/deepseekTools.mjs); both are called only by the control plane with this key, never by a runtime, held to `requestsPerSecond` per account for each tool, and billed per successful request -- a 200 with a result -- at `cnyPerThousandRequests` (the yuan table of DeepSeek's zh-cn Search guide, read 2026-10-17; the English page's USD 0.75 is the same price for dollar accounts; price list evimed-reference-2026-10-17).

js-yaml.notes: Required security backport for YAML4 CPU bounds. Workspace and both pinned kernel/profile copies must match this package without changing the DSH namespace. The runtime build hook is integrated, not pending: deploy/runtime-dsh/runtime-yaml-security.mjs runs in both runtime images (Dockerfile and Dockerfile.agentbay) -- `global` patches the globally installed kernel closure once it is installed, and `verify` re-checks that tree and the pre-initialized profile after the profile seed, including the seal -- and scripts/ops/kernel-install.mjs and deploy/runtime-dsh/profile-kernel-pins.mjs read this one pin (apps/server/test/runtimeYamlSecurity.test.mjs and dshProfileKernelPins.test.mjs hold it). Only the reviewed `js-yaml` and `zod` entries are accepted; moving it is one edit here, with the package's integrity.

zod.notes: Official Zod4 constrained collection issue bounds; replace complete package in global kernel and profile without changing kernel pins or publication cutoff. Zod3 physical installations are unsupported and refused.

openmed.notes: No SDK serving, local model runtime or weights. Native implementations use the existing cloud gateway and VCR stores. Dataset and terminology rights are reviewed separately.

loopx.notes: The complete native DSH plugin and CLI. Built into the immutable runtime with upstream workflow skills, GoalBar and same-session continuation. Hosted bootstrap checks installed bytes instead of upgrading during a turn; telemetry is disabled. Goal lifecycle belongs to LoopX; tenant ownership, model billing and clinical evidence remain EviMed responsibilities. Moved from 1.3.1 to 1.4.0 on 2026-10-17 (R19, r19-upstream2a) after real goals on the pinned kernel with a real model, the CLI and the skills root read-only and Node 22.22.3: /loopx starts a goal, the GoalBar shows it, Pause and Start change its state, a continuation turn runs (route loopx-continuation, automated, charged to the researcher), the inbox item arrives, a goal made by 1.3.1 opens, pauses and starts under 1.4.0, and a new goal's SQLite authority store (HOME/.loopx/authority/sqlite-v0) is read back by a fresh process; the evidence is in .evimed-local/acceptance/course-correction-20261012/live/r19-upstream2a/. What 1.4.0 asks of a runtime: Node >= 22.22.3 on PATH (see runtimeTools.node), the project's writable HOME and TMPDIR, and one long-lived effect-runtime process of about 25 MB, which does not exit when idle (1.3.1's did not either). The same on 1.3.1 and 1.4.0: a conversation opened on a cold kernel shows no GoalBar until the page is reloaded (its first read answers session_unavailable and is not retried; runtimeUiServer asks that read again while the kernel takes the session up, OPEN_SCIENCE_RUNTIME_GOALBAR_READ_WAIT_MS, deletable when the plugin retries), and a GoalBar Start or Pause can answer that LoopX is unreachable or did not sync when the CLI is slow (an action is up to four CLI calls; the proxy's admission gives it OPEN_SCIENCE_RUNTIME_GOALBAR_ACTION_TIMEOUT_MS, 60 s, where a prompt's 30 s used to cut it while the action went on). The kernel holds the driver in memory, so what happens to a goal around LoopX is the control plane's (researchGoalService.mjs, 2026-11-03): it takes up a goal a runtime or the provider interrupted, reads LoopX's bar to learn what a quiet goal came to, and pauses one through the bar after three rounds with no file or at its spend limit. To watch: after Pause pressed in a turn that then ends before its receipts are closed, 1.4.0 ran one automatic recovery turn while the goal was paused (1 of 2 samples; 1.3.1 ran none in 3; the recovery module is byte-identical in both, the entry skill is not). 1.4.1 and 1.4.2 (2026-10-15) are not adopted; adopting one is the same steps: a scratch install with install-loopx.mjs, the goal runs of r19-upstream2a/scripts/loopx-run.mjs, workflow-skills.json and this block. Both compatibility adaptations below act on the plugin archive, which did not move, and were seen working on 1.4.0 (the driver continued the goal; the pause note reached a busy model).

dshVersionExemption.reason: The plugin's peer range ends below DSH 0.2.1 (`>=0.2.0-rc.2 <0.2.1-0` for @deepseek-ai/dsh and six dsh-client-* packages) and 0.2.1 holds a bundle to that range at install and at every start: refused at `dsh plugin add`, skipped whole from a profile that has no exemption. No newer plugin exists (the release list and the plugin's package.json on loopx-project/loopx main name the same range on 2026-10-17). Run on a live 0.2.1-rc.2 kernel with a real model before this record was written: the GoalBar, a goal started with /loopx, its continuation turn and pause (.evimed-local/acceptance/course-correction-20261012/live/r19-dsh021/). Run again on 0.2.1-rc.5 before the pair was moved (2026-11-01): the GoalBar, a goal started with /loopx, its pause and resume, a continuation turn and the inbox note.
dshVersionExemption.upgradePath: Granted at image build by deploy/runtime-dsh/loopx-compat.mjs --grant-exemption through the kernel's own `dsh plugin allow-version … --accept-risk` (the profile's compatibility.json, carried to every project volume by profile-seed.mjs), only for this exact pair and only for the archive whose sha256 is loopx.plugin.sha256; a moved kernel or plugin pin fails the build by name until the pair is run again and recorded. Drop this record when a plugin release declares a range that includes the DSH pin.

skillEdit.reason: The CLI's `loopx-project` skill, which the model's catalogue keeps (packages/contracts/loopx/workflow-skills.json), tells the model to "prefer loopx-doc-registry" in its description line (every session's catalogue), to "load `loopx-doc-registry`" in its first paragraph, and calls it the "trigger" of its authority-registration section: a skill this image leaves out with the other five repository-management workflows (the 2026-10-17 narrowing). Found on the integrated acceptance of 2026-10-17 (r19-accepta, finding 7); the alternative, keeping that skill, would add its own description to the catalogue, and that line says "Use even when the user does not mention LoopX or doc registry", which would pull ordinary note-taking into a LoopX project registry. The three pointers are taken out and nothing else in the file changes: the section's commands (`loopx register-authority-source`, `loopx import-doc-registry-authority`) are the CLI's and stay.
skillEdit.upgradePath: A build-time, digest-bound edit of the folder the CLI installs (deploy/runtime-dsh/install-loopx.mjs adaptLoopxProjectSkill, after the unkept folders are removed): it applies only to the SKILL.md whose sha256 is the one above (the wheel's own, equal to what the CLI writes), needs each of the three fragments exactly once, and must produce the file whose sha256 is adaptedSha256; anything else fails the image build by name. The CLI's readback manifest (.loopx-skill-install.json) is written back for the folder, as the CLI would have, so its own check still passes, and installation.json records the edit beside the digests of what upstream shipped. Drop it, and this record, when a CLI release no longer names loopx-doc-registry in loopx-project, or when the kept set includes that skill (a decision about its catalogue cost, scripts/ops/skill-catalogue-size.mjs, and about its description). Re-read on every CLI pin change.

compatibility.reason: Accept the recorded tool-role activation envelope of pinned DSH 0.1.7. After a verified GoalBar pause, explain the user action to the current model step without waking an idle session.
compatibility.upgradePath: Both adaptations are build-time, digest-bound edits of the pinned plugin archive (deploy/runtime-dsh/loopx-compat.mjs); a changed byte fails the image build by name. Drop the driver adaptation when the plugin pin recognizes the DSH 0.1.7 tool-role result, or when the DSH pin moves to a kernel that records the user/tool-result envelope; drop the pause adaptation when the GoalBar itself tells a busy model that its owner paused the goal. Re-record packages/contracts/loopx/goalbar-locale.json on any plugin pin change.
